docs.title: Aquamatrix SIMAR MCP Server
docs.text:
An async Model Context Protocol server for reading billing information from the SIMAR customer portal through the independent Aquamatrix SIMAR Python SDK.

The server is unofficial, read-only, and not affiliated with SIMAR or Aquamatrix.

docs.title: Tools
docs.text:
• get_invoices: retrieve one page of invoice history with optional date filters.
  • get_pending_invoices: retrieve invoices the SDK recognizes as unpaid.
  • get_billing_summary: retrieve the portal's invoice-to-pay and failed-invoice counts.

Money values are decimal strings and calendar dates use ISO YYYY-MM-DD format. Credentials are configured through the server environment, not exposed as tool inputs.

docs.text:

docs.title: Docker Compose
docs.text: The supplied Dockerfile builds a small Python 3.14 image, installs the published package metadata from the local source tree, runs as a non-root user, and starts the server using Streamable HTTP. The Compose file binds the application inside its container network but publishes the host port only on 127.0.0.1.

docs.title: Start
docs.text:
Pass credentials via environment variables:

export SIMAR_NIF='your-nif'
export SIMAR_PASSWORD='your-password'
docker compose up --build -d

Alternatively, create a local .env file (ignored by .dockerignore and .gitignore) and restrict its filesystem permissions. Never commit it:

SIMAR_NIF=your-nif
SIMAR_PASSWORD=your-password
SIMAR_BASE_URL=https://www.aquamatrix.pt
MCP_PORT=8000

Then run:

docker compose up --build -d
docker compose logs --follow

The endpoint is http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp. Stop the service with docker compose down.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Compose reads SIMAR_NIF and SIMAR_PASSWORD as required variables. SIMAR_BASE_URL and MCP_PORT may be set in the shell or .env; the remaining HTTP settings are declared by Compose for container networking.

The container sets MCP_ALLOW_NON_LOOPBACK=true because its HTTP server must listen on the container interface. This opt-in is paired with host-only loopback port publishing. Do not change the published address to 0.0.0.0 or expose the container port to an untrusted network: this service has no HTTP authentication.

For production deployment, prefer your orchestrator's secret manager over a checked-in or broadly readable .env file.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.14 or newer.
  • An authorized SIMAR portal account.

Install from PyPI:

python -m pip install aquamatrix-simar-mcp

Provide credentials to the server process using environment variables:

export SIMAR_NIF='your-nif'
export SIMAR_PASSWORD='your-password'
aquamatrix-simar-mcp

The server does not persist credentials. Keep them out of source files, shell history where possible, tool arguments, logs, and issue reports. For managed deployment, use the platform's secret/environment facility.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Variable Default Meaning SIMAR_NIF Required SIMAR account NIF SIMAR_PASSWORD Required SIMAR account password SIMAR_BASE_URL https://www.aquamatrix.pt HTTPS base URL for the portal MCP_TRANSPORT stdio stdio or streamable-http MCP_HOST 127.0.0.1 HTTP bind address; loopback by default MCP_ALLOW_NON_LOOPBACK false Explicitly allows non-loopback binding MCP_PORT 8000 HTTP port, from 1 to 65535

MCP_ALLOW_NON_LOOPBACK=true disables the loopback bind guard. It is intended for container network namespaces and is not an authentication mechanism. Keep the host-side port private, or provide a separately reviewed authenticated and encrypted proxy before remote access.

docs.title: GitHub Pages setup
docs.text: The documentation.yml workflow builds the MkDocs site for pull requests and deploys it after pushes to main or a manual workflow run. In repository settings, choose Pages → Build and deployment → Source → GitHub Actions. The site URL is https://oldemarjesus.github.io/aquamatrix-python-mcp/.

docs.title: PyPI trusted publishing setup
docs.text:
Configure the publisher once:

  1. Create the aquamatrix-simar-mcp project on PyPI or open its publishing settings.
  2. Add a pending trusted publisher with owner OldemarJesus, repository aquamatrix-python-mcp, workflow filename publish.yml, and environment pypi.
  3. Create a GitHub repository environment named pypi. Add protection/approval rules if appropriate.
  4. Update project.version in pyproject.toml, run checks, and commit the release.
  5. Create and publish a GitHub Release with a matching version tag, for example v0.1.0.

The workflow verifies that the release tag matches the package version, runs tests/lint/type checks, builds the source and wheel distributions, and publishes the validated artifacts using GitHub OIDC. No PyPI API token is stored as a GitHub secret.

PyPI versions are immutable. For a failed or already-published version, fix the issue and release a new version rather than reusing the same one.

docs.title: Credentials and logs
docs.text:
Credentials are read from environment variables at server startup and remain in process memory for the client lifetime. They are not MCP arguments, stored persistently, or intentionally logged. SDK operation failures are translated to generic tool messages so upstream exception text, credentials, and personal billing data are not returned to the MCP client or emitted through exception tracebacks.

Hosts and deployment platforms may capture process output independently. Restrict log access and do not enable HTTP wire/debug logging around account operations. Avoid sharing logs, environment dumps, container inspection output, or unredacted diagnostic captures.

docs.title: Network boundary
docs.text: stdio is the preferred local-host transport. Streamable HTTP binds to loopback by default and has no authentication. The explicit MCP_ALLOW_NON_LOOPBACK=true option only changes the bind-address guard; it does not secure the service. The Compose example maps the host port to loopback. Remote hosting requires an independently reviewed authentication, TLS, and authorization boundary.

docs.title: Read-only scope and upstream limits
docs.text:
The tools only retrieve billing data. They do not submit payments, modify account details, automate a browser, or bypass CAPTCHA/MFA. Aquamatrix's portal is not a documented stable API, so behavior can change; the upstream SDK owns protocol handling and reports failures through stable errors.

This is an unofficial project and is not affiliated with or endorsed by SIMAR or Aquamatrix. Use it only with an account you are authorized to access and in accordance with applicable terms.

docs.title: get_invoices
docs.text:
Returns one page of invoices. start is a zero-based offset (0 by default), and limit is between 1 and 500 (100 by default). Optional date_from and date_to values use YYYY-MM-DD and are inclusive. A reversed date range is rejected.

Invoice output includes document number/type, year, issue and payment dates, exact amount as a decimal string, portal state, payment date, client code when available, and the SDK's pending classification.

docs.title: get_pending_invoices
docs.text: Returns invoices the SDK classifies as pending. The SDK owns the portal-state mapping and payment-status logic.

docs.title: get_billing_summary
docs.text:
Returns invoices_to_pay and failed_invoices counts.

All three tools are annotated as read-only. No tool accepts credentials or performs account mutations or payments.

docs.title: stdio
docs.text:
stdio is the default for local MCP hosts that launch the server as a subprocess:

aquamatrix-simar-mcp

The host must provide SIMAR_NIF and SIMAR_PASSWORD in the server process environment. Do not print diagnostics to stdout; stdio carries MCP protocol messages.

docs.title: Streamable HTTP
docs.text:
For an HTTP MCP client, run:

MCP_TRANSPORT=streamable-http aquamatrix-simar-mcp

The endpoint defaults to http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp. HTTP has no server authentication, so loopback is the supported default. SSE is not provided; Streamable HTTP is the current standard transport.
